If Ta’zir means discretion, discretion must include the Prophetic mercy that sought to avert the harshest punishment where possible. On Ta’zir and Proportionality This was not a Hadd punishment for Zina, which requires four eyewitnesses to the actual act. It was Ta’zir – discretionary punishment for a grave act that the court deemed deserving of death for violating the holiness of Makkah. And that is precisely where the global scholarly debate is needed. Ta’zir, by its classical definition, is meant to be corrective, deterrent, and proportionate to the offence and offender – lashes, imprisonment, exile, fines, according to many jurists, with death as Ta’zir being the most disputed and restricted application. These are not questions to be answered by social media outrage or by state press releases. They are questions for qualified fuqaha. We do not call for condoning fahisha in the House of Allah. We call for scholarly ijtihad that shows the world that Islamic law is not bloodthirsty, but profound – that it defends sanctity while preserving life, that it punishes desecration while leaving the door of Tawbah open. The viral lies about a “kiss” insulted our intelligence. But a routine acceptance of death for every grave Ta’zir without scholarly debate insults our fiqh. Let the League of Muftis convene. item.title: Abduction of corps members: DSS arraigns three suspects, two others
item.description: By Emmanuel Iheaka The Department of State Services has arraigned three suspects, namely Usman Aliyu, Babangida Aliyu and Mohammed Ali, over the kidnapping of 20 NYSC corps members along the Owerri-Onitsha road. The three suspects pleaded not guilty to the three-count charge of abduction and hostage taking, collection of ransom of N48 million and dollars, as well as illegal possession of firearms. The other two suspects, Aminu Haliru and Jiji Ibrahim, were charged with conspiracy and hostage-taking, and illegal possession of firearms. They were accused of abducting Winner Ogidi, Opara Timothy, Ogechi Henrietta and one other on October 4, 2026, but they also pleaded not guilty to the charges. Counsel for the state, Ekezie Nwauzo, filed a motion for the suspects to remain in the DSS custody, which the court presided over by Hon. Justice Emeka Orafu granted. Nnaemeka Adipuo stood for the first and second defendants in the case of abduction of corps members, while Paschal Ofoma represented the third defendant. The cases were adjourned to Thursday, October 22; Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday, October 27, 28, 29, for hearing. Recall that about 20 corps members had been reportedly abducted on October 1, along Owerri-Onitsha Road, while heading to the NYSC orientation camps in Akwa Ibom and Abia States. They were later released after about six days in captivity and subsequently reunited with their families. Speaking to journalists after the court session, counsels for the defendants, Adipuo and Ofoma, noted that the suspects are presumed innocent until proven guilty. item.title: SDP to scrap bulletproof SUVs, charter jets for officials – Adebayo
item.description: By John Alechenu Presidential candidate of the Social Democratic Party, SDP, Prince Adewole Adebayo, has vowed to scrap bulletproof SUVs, charter flights and other luxury perks for public officials if elected, describing the current system as Nigerians subsidising political opulence. In a statement by the Chief Media and Communications Adviser of the Adebayo-Bugaje Presidential Campaign, Comrade Mark Adebayo, in Abuja, on Tuesday. The SDP candidate said an SDP administration will redirect trillions of Naira wasted on executive comforts into education, healthcare and infrastructure. “We will stop Nigerians from subsidizing the lavish lifestyles of politicians,” Adebayo declared, noting that hardship in the country is not due to lack of resources but a ruling class that “prioritizes institutionalized waste over human capital development.” Adebayo explained that successive budgets have funnelled enormous public capital into luxury vehicles, presidential fleet upgrades, State House renovations and loosely defined empowerment schemes while families grapple with inflation, fuel duty increases and crumbling social services. According to fiscal estimates cited from civil society tracking reports and budget analyses, the cost of political opulence runs into multiple trillions annually, with nearly N1 trillion regularly earmarked across cycles for luxury utility vehicles, presidential fleet upgrades and executive renovations. Mid-2026 budget implementation updates, he added, show that 33 state governments expended over $300 million, about N410 billion, on governors’ offices, Government Houses and executive travel within six months, indicating an annual drain exceeding N1 trillion across all 36 states. Adebayo also condemned multi-billion Naira deviations for luxury armoured vehicles, including single-agency procurements exceeding N10 billion for management fleets and state purchases outside appropriation bills, which he described as “criminal wastes in the midst of mass suffering induced by the anti-people policies of the current APC administration.” He assured that an SDP government will plug the leakages, eliminate unconstitutional vehicle allowances and restructure public finances, insisting four years is sufficient for a determined leader to fix infrastructure in line with Nigeria’s history of focused governance. The party urged Nigerians to reject leaders who treat public resources as personal accounts and embrace an economic model centred on welfare, production and transparent service delivery. item.title: ‘He let Manchester United down’ – Ten Hag recounts fallout with Ronaldo
item.description: Former Manchester United manager Erik ten Hag has accused Cristiano Ronaldo of letting both the club and him down during their time together at Old Trafford, alleging that the Portuguese forward failed to meet the team’s fitness and training standards. Ten Hag made the remarks in an exclusive interview with The Athletic on Tuesday, reflecting on his difficult relationship with the five-time Ballon d’Or winner during his tenure as United manager. “He let the team down, and he let me down, because we planned with him,” Ten Hag said. “I flew out to Portugal to speak with him about what I was aiming for before I came to United.” Despite his criticism, the Dutchman acknowledged Ronaldo’s place in football history, describing him as one of the game’s greatest players. “Obviously, he’s one of the best in football history. I respected him a lot. But at that time, as a manager, I had to make a rational decision,” he added. Ten Hag also alleged that Ronaldo struggled to meet the club’s fitness requirements, claiming that the forward sometimes withdrew from training sessions and failed to achieve the required heart rate levels. He also recalled an incident after United’s 4-0 defeat to Brentford in August 2022, when players had to run laps as punishment. According to Ten Hag, Ronaldo completed only two of the three laps. The former manager said he confronted Ronaldo over his fitness and positioning, insisting that the forward needed to work harder to put himself in scoring positions. “I confronted him with this,” Ten Hag said. “Many times I say, ‘Ronnie, everyone wants to work for you to bring you in the right position, but if you can’t bring yourself in the box, you can’t score’. He was not capable to do this.” Ten Hag also claimed that Ronaldo did not contribute sufficiently to the team’s pressing and defensive work, alleging that the forward encouraged teammates to conserve their energy during training. “Ronaldo was telling the players: save your legs at training,” he said. “I understand it when you are top fit, but first you have to train yourself to get into the right fitness levels.” The Dutchman maintained that while managers must accommodate their best players, star footballers must also accept their responsibilities to the team. “Every top team has to embrace the top player, but the top player has to work for the team,” Ten Hag said. Ronaldo’s relationship with Ten Hag deteriorated during the 2022/23 season, culminating in the forward’s departure from Manchester United in November 2022 following a controversial interview in which he criticised the club and its management. I respected him a lot. But at that time, as a manager, I had to make a rational decision,” he added. Ten Hag also alleged that Ronaldo struggled to meet the club’s fitness requirements, claiming that the forward sometimes withdrew from training sessions and failed to achieve the required heart rate levels. He also recalled an incident after United’s 4-0 defeat to Brentford in August 2022, when players had to run laps as punishment. According to Ten Hag, Ronaldo completed only two of the three laps. The former manager said he confronted Ronaldo over his fitness and positioning, insisting that the forward needed to work harder to put himself in scoring positions. “I confronted him with this,” Ten Hag said. “Many times I say, ‘Ronnie, everyone wants to work for you to bring you in the right position, but if you can’t bring yourself in the box, you can’t score’. He was not capable to do this.” Ten Hag also claimed that Ronaldo did not contribute sufficiently to the team’s pressing and defensive work, alleging that the forward encouraged teammates to conserve their energy during training. “Ronaldo was telling the players: save your legs at training,” he said. “I understand it when you are top fit, but first you have to train yourself to get into the right fitness levels.” The Dutchman maintained that while managers must accommodate their best players, star footballers must also accept their responsibilities to the team. “Every top team has to embrace the top player, but the top player has to work for the team,” Ten Hag said. Ronaldo’s relationship with Ten Hag deteriorated during the 2022/23 season, culminating in the forward’s departure from Manchester United in November 2022 following a controversial interview in which he criticised the club and its management. item.title: China opposes US ban on govt agencies from using DeepSeek
item.description: Beijing opposed on Tuesday a US government ban on its agencies using AI tools from Chinese startup DeepSeek, saying the move “overstretched” the concept of national security. China and the United States are locked in a race for dominance in the fast-moving artificial intelligence sector, trading accusations of stealing AI technologies and jeopardising security in recent months. The US Department of Homeland Security on Monday banned products developed by DeepSeek — and tools created using DeepSeek by third parties — saying they risked sharing sensitive data with China. Beijing’s foreign ministry opposed the ban on Tuesday, vowing to protect Chinese businesses. “China has consistently opposed the overstretching of the concept of national security and the politicisation of issues related to science, technology, and trade,” ministry spokesperson Mao Ning told a news conference. The Department of Homeland Security can issue directions to civilian agencies, but not the military or intelligence services. Its statement on Monday said that “DeepSeek’s models multiple threat vectors” and must be removed from IT devices. Use of DeepSeek AI tools “may result in the transfer of sensitive data to (China) if used by US government employees or vendors,” the department warned. Its servers are located in China, where the legal system permits the government “extensive authority” to access private company infrastructure, it said. AFP has contacted DeepSeek for comment. DeepSeek, one of China’s top AI labs, shook up the industry in January 2025 with a low-cost, high-performance chatbot, challenging assumptions of US dominance. The firm released a long-awaited new model, V4, in April and this month updated a faster, more lightweight version of V4. The United States has accused DeepSeek and other top Chinese AI firms of systematically stealing the capabilities of cutting-edge models developed by American rivals. Despite their fierce competition in the field, China and the United States in September agreed to set up a “communication channel” for AI incidents. The topic is expected to arise again when the countries’ leaders meet next month at a summit in the Chinese city of Shenzhen. item.title: Troops rescue 27 kidnapped victims in Katsina, recover motorcycles
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of Operation Fansan Yamma have recorded another operational success with the rescue of 27 kidnapped victims and recovery of a motorcycle in Katsina State. Lieutenant Colonel Aliyu Danja, Media Information Officer, made this known on Tuesday, noting that the successful operations underscore the sustained offensive posture and operational effectiveness of troops of Operation Fansan Yamma. He said, “On 16 October 2026, troops of Sector 1 received a distress call on terrorist activities in Gamji community, Sabuwa Local Government Area. “It was reported that terrorists had abducted 27 residents, comprising 15 males and 12 females. “Troops responded swiftly, pursuing the terrorists along the Gangare–Kamba axis. “On contact, troops engaged with superior firepower, forcing the terrorists to abandon their victims and flee in disarray. “All 27 victims were rescued unharmed during exploitation of the area. “They have been profiled and handed over to community leaders for reunification with their families. “In a separate operation on the same day, troops conducting fighting patrol around Kurba village in Kankara Local Government Area encountered terrorists on 3 motorcycles. “The terrorists fled on sighting troops, abandoning one motorcycle. “The successful operations underscore the sustained offensive posture and operational effectiveness of troops of Operation Fansan Yamma in denying terrorists freedom of action and safeguarding vulnerable communities across the Joint Operations Area. “The Theatre Commander, Joint Task Force North West, Operation Fansan Yamma, commends troops for their gallantry and swift response. “He assures residents of Katsina, Zamfara and adjoining states of the Task Force’s unwavering commitment to restoring lasting peace and security.” The post Troops rescue 27 kidnapped victims in Katsina, recover motorcycles appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: ‘Suarez killed Africa’s hope’ — Ghana’s Ayew revisits 2010 handball incident
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Ghana forward Andre Ayew has recalled the heartbreak of the 2010 FIFA World Cup quarter-final against Uruguay, saying Luis Suarez’s handball denied not only Ghana but the entire African continent a chance to reach the semi-finals then. Ayew spoke on the Obi One Podcast released on Monday, reflecting on Ghana’s dramatic elimination at the tournament in South Africa. “And Luis Suarez handling that ball killed a lot of hopes, not just from Ghana, but the whole continent,” he said. Ayew recalled that Ghana’s players had been confident of beating Uruguay and reaching the final. “How are we not going to beat Uruguay? It was not in our heads, to be honest. We were like, As soon as we beat Uruguay, we’re going to face Holland,” he said. “If we get to the semi-finals, we’re going to the finals. There was this belief that having the whole of South Africa behind us.” Ayew, who was in the stands during the match, said the handball initially left him furious, particularly as he was still a teenager at the time. “Then Suarez catches this ball. I was in the stands, and I was like, ‘I’m young, 19 or 20; everything is just flying up.’ What’s going on? He’s an idiot; he’s this, he’s that,” he recalled. He said the players were devastated when Gyan missed the penalty but did not blame the striker, whom they regarded as a key reason Ghana had reached that stage of the competition. “The players were not angry at the situation of Baby Jet or whatever. We were more like, If you were not there, we wouldn’t get here,” Ayew said, referring to Gyan by his nickname. He described Gyan as Ghana’s designated penalty taker and said the striker had enjoyed an outstanding tournament before the decisive moment. Ayew added that he still sometimes watches the match but avoids watching the penalty shootout because of Ghana’s record in such contests, including the AFCON. Ghana faced Uruguay in Johannesburg on July 2, 2010. The match ended 1-1 after extra time, with Ghana coming close to winning it in the final moments. item.title: UPDATED: DSS Arraigns Five Suspects Over Kidnap Of 20 Corps Members, Others In Imo
item.description: The Department of State Services (DSS) has arraigned five suspects allegedly linked to the abduction of 20 prospective National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) members and a civilian along the Owerri–Onitsha Expressway in Imo State. The suspects were brought before the Justice Oputa State High Court in Owerri, the state capital, following their arrest during intelligence-led operations in Rivers and Abia states. ﻿ The victims were abducted by gunmen near Umunoha in Mbaitoli Local Government Area on October 1, 2026, while travelling from Ibadan, Oyo State, to their assigned NYSC orientation camps in Abia and Akwa Ibom states. The abduction sparked a security operation to locate the victims and apprehend those responsible. On October 7, the 20 prospective corps members and the civilian were rescued from the Amakohia-Ubi forest in Owerri West Local Government Area. They subsequently received medical attention at the DSS hospital in Owerri. The DSS later arrested five suspects in intelligence-led operations conducted between October 10 and 14 in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, and Aba, Abia State. The operations involved a joint security team led by the DSS, working with the military, police and other security operatives. Three other suspects reportedly escaped with gunshot wounds, prompting a manhunt for them and other fleeing members of the suspected kidnapping syndicate. The arraignment marks a further step in the investigation into the abduction, as the prosecution of the five arrested suspects gets underway. item.title: INEC chairman warns staff against partisan politics
item.description: …promises new salary structure By Chinedu Adonu The Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Amupitan (SAN), has warned staff of the commission against partisan politics, urging them to maintain neutrality and professionalism in the discharge of their electoral duties. Amupitan gave the warning on Monday during an interactive session with INEC staff from the South-East region shortly after arriving in Enugu on a working visit to engage traditional rulers and electoral stakeholders in the zone. He said the commission would not tolerate unethical conduct or actions capable of undermining public confidence in the electoral process. “You should not pick interest in any political party. Be neutral and firm. I am hearing that some of you are showing interest in some political parties. This is absolutely wrong. “The commission wants you to be neutral and professional, both in your words and actions. The commission will not tolerate unprofessional or unethical electoral conduct from any staff,” he said. The INEC chairman disclosed that the commission had introduced a reward and sanction mechanism covering its local government, state and national offices to promote discipline and accountability among personnel. He also announced plans to move INEC staff from the conventional civil service salary structure to a special salary structure, which he said would take effect from January 1, 2027. According to him, the initiative is aimed at improving staff welfare and reducing the likelihood of electoral officials being induced before, during and after elections. “We want the new salary structure so that you will not easily be induced before, during and after election. We are working with other relevant governmental agencies and commissions to make the cash backing for the new salary structure possible,” he said. Amupitan urged staff to work diligently to restore and strengthen public confidence in the commission, stressing that their conduct was critical to the credibility of elections. “As an unbiased umpire, we need to improve the confidence and trust the people repose in us by being disciplined and diligent in the discharge of our duties at all times,” he said. In preparations for the forthcoming general election, the INEC chairman disclosed that the commission had provided its Enugu office with 10 new pickup vans, adding that more logistics would be made available. He said non-sensitive election materials were ready, while contracts for other required materials, including sensitive materials, were being processed. “Massive training and retraining will commence soon. The retraining is imperative, given the new guidelines and regulations introduced into the amended Electoral Act,” he added. item.title: Why Gov Otu deserves second term- Obono-Obla
item.description: A former presidential aide and chieftain of the All Progressives Congress, Okoi Obono-Obla is confident that Governor Bassey Otu of Cross River State will win his second term election by a landslide. Obono-Obla who was speaking on Arise News programme NewsNight, hinged his confidence on what he described as the Governor’s performance and management of the state’s finances. While stating that opposition in the state has been weakened by internal strife, he said Otu inherited a state facing significant financial challenges, including substantial debt and difficulties paying workers’ salaries. According to him, Otu has managed to address these challenges creditably well without resort to borrowing. He also highlighted an increase in the state’s internally generated revenue (IGR), stating that it rose from approximately ₦21 billion in 2022 to nearly ₦76 billion in 2026. Obono-Obla maintained that Governor Otu’s handling of the state’s financial challenges, efforts to improve internally generated revenue, and overall performance makes his re-election a foregone conclusion. On efforts by opposition parties to present a single presidential candidate against President Bola Tinubu, he dismissed the idea as a mere comic relief. item.description: A former National Commissioner for Information and Voter Education at the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Festus Okoye, has accused Nigeria’s political elite of seeking to undermine voters’ power through vote-buying. Speaking on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief on Tuesday, Okoye said the political elite appeared unwilling to allow Nigerians to freely choose their leaders, lamenting that they wanted to take away the people’s power to determine election outcomes. “I think that political elite in this country really do not believe in free, fair, and transparent election. They just want to buy the votes of the people. They want to replace the people as the sovereign, and it is very unfortunate,” Okoye said. ﻿ He said a credible election should allow voters to cast their ballots without intimidation, coercion or duress. Okoye lamented that political parties lacked clear ideologies and were not campaigning on issues, accusing them of seeking ways to ensure that votes did not count on election day. “The mark of a free, fair and transparent election is the ability of the people to go to the polling units to cast their votes without any form of intimidation, without any form of coercion, and without any form of duress. “But in this country, what we are now having is a situation where political parties have no ideologies, political parties are not campaigning on any issue, all they know is that on election day they will find a way of making sure that the votes of the people really do not count.” On the use of technology in elections, Okoye called for continued improvements in the electoral process and the deployment of technology when appropriate. He also urged the media, civil society organisations and Nigerians to pay close attention to the activities of the political elite before, during and after elections. “I think that what is important is for the country to keep on improving and also keep on deploying technology as at when due in our electoral process. “But more importantly, I think the media, civil society groups and organisations, and the Nigerian people generally must focus attention on the activities of the political elite before, during and after election.” Okoye noted that ad hoc staff, including members of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) and other Nigerians recruited for elections, play a more prominent role in conducting elections at polling units than INEC’s regular staff. item.title: Police smash suspected robbery gang, arrest six in Jigawa
item.description: ‎‎By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse ‎The Jigawa State Police Command has arrested six suspected members of an armed robbery gang responsible for attacks on residents of Jahun Local Government Area, during which cash, mobile phones and other valuables worth millions of naira were stolen. The command’s public relations officer, SP Lawan Shiisu Adam, disclosed this in a statement issued to journalists on Monday. ‎He said the arrests followed investigations into two armed robbery incidents reported in Jahun on September 24, 2026. ‎According to him, the gang invaded the residence of a 35-year-old man in Kofar Daru Quarters at about 2:00 a.m., making away with ₦20.18 million in cash, iTel mobile phones valued at ₦13.13 million, recharge cards worth ₦1 million, Android phones and other valuables. ‎He explained that the suspects also attacked the residence of a 37-year-old man in Shagari Quarters, where they stole ₦45,000, two blankets, rice and a woman’s wrapper. ‎Shiisu said detectives from Jahun Police Division immediately launched an investigation, which led to the arrest of five suspects. ‎He identified them as Sale Ibrahim, 25; Abubakar Abdullahi, 28; Babangida Ya’u, 35; Babannan Hassan, 27; and Isah Isibu, 35. ‎The police spokesperson said another breakthrough was recorded on October 15, 2026, when operatives of Maigatari Police Division, in collaboration with the Border Patrol Team, arrested a sixth suspect during a routine patrol at Maigatari Market. ‎The suspect identified as Isa Yusuf, 35, from Hantsu village in Miga Local Government Area, was found in possession of 13 new iTel mobile phones, 13 chargers, 13 batteries and ₦102,500 in cash. ‎He said the suspect was transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID) in Dutse for further investigation. ‎According to Shiisu, the suspect confessed during interrogation to being a member of the gang involved in the Jahun robbery incidents. ‎He added that further investigation linked the recovered mobile phones and other items to the property stolen during the attacks. ‎The police spokesperson said all six suspects had been charged to court, while efforts were ongoing to track down other fleeing members of the gang and recover the remaining stolen property. ‎ The post Police smash suspected robbery gang, arrest six in Jigawa appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Anambra confirms Lassa fever case, activates emergency response
item.description: The Anambra Government has confirmed a Lassa fever case involving a patient linked to Omasi in Ayamelum Local Government Area (LGA), who is currently receiving treatment at the Federal Teaching Hospital, Abakaliki (FETHA), Ebonyi. The State Commissioner for Health, Dr Afam Obidike, disclosed this on Monday at an emergency stakeholders’ meeting in Awka. Obidike said the state had activated an emergency response to prevent further transmission. “The state has intensified disease surveillance and public awareness. “The meeting, attended by health partners, including the World Health Organisation and Médecins Sans Frontières, led to the activation of the Incident Management System. “Health officials will follow up on the affected household in Omasi, identify people who had contact with the patient and classify them according to their level of exposure for appropriate monitoring,” he said. The commissioner urged residents experiencing persistent fever or malaria-like symptoms that do not improve with appropriate treatment to seek medical attention promptly. He warned against relying solely on self-medication, stressing that early diagnosis and proper medical care were essential to managing the disease. Also speaking, the State Epidemiologist, Dr Chuma Emembolu, advised residents to keep food covered and store it in rodent-proof containers to prevent contamination by rats. Emembolu also urged residents to maintain clean surroundings and prevent rodents from contaminating food and household items with their urine and droppings. He further warned against direct contact with the blood and other body fluids of suspected or confirmed Lassa fever patients. The epidemiologist called for strict compliance with infection prevention measures and the guidance of health professionals. “We urge residents of Omasi and other communities in Ayamelum and the state at large to remain vigilant, cooperate with public health officials and avoid spreading unverified information. “These measures are aimed at strengthening preparedness, monitoring potential contacts and reducing the risk of further transmission,” he said. With domestic and international matches coming thick and fast, Kane has not had time to exchange pleasantries with any of his Gunners rivals. “I spoke to them a bit in the international break previously and we knew the game was coming up, but I think we’re all too busy right now to text each other, with a game every three days,” he explained. In the recent changes at INEC, Mrs Oluyemi Titilayo Adeyemi-Showunmi, formerly the Administrative Secretary of the commission’s Lagos State office, was redeployed as the Director of Electoral Operations at the commission. She is the wife of Segun Showunmi, a spokesman for the Tinubu/Shettima 2027 Presidential Campaign Council. According to reports, Isah Magaji Gummi, who previously headed the Electoral Operations Department, was redeployed to the Voter Registry Department. Although the director of the department does not independently determine election results, the responsibilities attached to the office have drawn attention to the redeployment and calls for INEC to explain the considerations behind the decision. Adeyemi-Showunmi’s redeployment has sparked debate among civil society organisations and on social media over transparency, political neutrality and public confidence in the electoral body. Former director of voter education at INEC, Mr Nick Dazang, when contacted said, it would be wrong for the Commission to pretend that appointing someone that close to a sitting governor who is contesting elections has no implications. “The person may be eminently qualified but I have profound misgivings if he can discharge or execute his office as Resident Electoral Commissioner with the professionalism, neutrality and impartiality that the office demands. On the redeployment of Sowunmi wife, he said in the time past, and oblivious of the closeness/proximity of INEC officials to certain politically exposed persons, INEC officials on their merit, had been inadvertently assigned to roles/tasks that put them in difficult positions which complicated the Commission’s core values of impartiality and neutrality. He said In such circumstances, and in deference to its core values, INEC has demonstrated sensitivity by not posting such deserving officials to these positions. “It is likely that the Commission may not be aware or cognizant of the said officer’s relationship with a prominent politician. “But once this is established, and its attention is called to this reality, it should promptly do the needful, namely: not to put the officer in a position that compromises the Commission’s principles of neutrality and provision of a level playing field to all contestants. In the prevailing circumstance, the officer should be directed to recuse herself. This will allay fears, rightly or wrongly, that she has been procured to deliberately confer an advantage to any candidate(s) in the election. Either the tenure of the subsisting Director is specially extended for the period of the election, or his Deputy is directed to act in the position of Director, subject to consideration(s) of merit, federal character and the core values aforementioned,” he added. Director-General of YIAGA Africa, Samson Itodo, warned that the electoral body must ensure public confidence in the electoral process and should not take the people for granted in its appointment. On the appointment of Adeyemi-Showunmi as INEC Director of Electoral Operations, Itodo said elections are fundamentally about operations, adding that by this token, it is one of the most sensitive and consequential departments within INEC. He said, “In fact, the Electoral Operations Department is at the heart of election administration. From the recruitment and deployment of polling officials to the planning, production and distribution of election materials, as well as the operational arrangements for voting and results collation, the department plays a central role in determining how elections are conducted. “Mrs. Showunmi’s competence and professional capacity are not in doubt. However, competence alone is not sufficient for appointments to sensitive positions in election management. The independence, impartiality and perceived neutrality of those entrusted with managing elections are equally important. “Appointing individuals with strong ties to politicians in such strategic positions inevitably raises legitimate questions about impartiality and INEC independence. These concerns become even more pronounced in a climate of deep public distrust, growing fears of political capture of INEC, and politicians boldly declaring the number of votes they expect to secure before a single ballot has been cast. “At a time when public confidence in the electoral process is already fragile, appointments to critical positions within INEC should inspire confidence, not deepen suspicion. INEC must recognize that its credibility rests not only on the technical competence of its personnel but also on public confidence in INEC’s independence from partisan interests. Public confidence in the electoral process must never be taken for granted. In this instance, it is being taken for granted,” he said. Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar was among those who first raised the alarm over the issue, demanding immediate and full transparency from INEC. In a statement issued by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, Atiku said the reported changes in the Electoral Operations Department raised serious questions that INEC must answer without delay. “Reports indicate that Director Isa Magaji Gummi was moved from Electoral Operations to the Voter Registry Department, while Mrs Oluyemi Titilayo Adeyemi-Showunmi was appointed to head Electoral Operations. Dr Lawrence Bayode has also been identified as the head of Information and Communication Technology (ICT). “These departments are at the heart of election administration. INEC must explain these decisions, publish the criteria applied and show that every appointment and redeployment followed due process, was based on merit and was free from political interference. Nigerians will not accept vague assurances on matters this serious.” Atiku said no official should be presumed compromised because of their ethnicity, background or associations. But when reported political connections or a concentration of appointments raises public concern, INEC must provide verifiable assurances that its impartiality is protected. “A government that has driven millions of Nigerians into hardship must not be allowed to turn the electoral umpire into an instrument of political survival. When sensitive election departments are reshaped and major contracts are surrounded by unanswered questions, the suspicion that a failing administration is seeking every possible advantage to cling to power will only grow. INEC must dispel that suspicion through full, immediate and verifiable disclosure,” he said.
